locator: Greenpeace International report, pp. 9–11, sections « Methodology » and « Results — Microplastics »
summary: SINTEF Ocean analysed three Nestlé Gerber yoghurt pouches and three Danone fruit-puree pouches purchased online. The report states that microplastics were detected in all food subsamples; for Nestlé yoghurt it reports up to 54 particles per gram on average and estimates more than 5,000 particles per pouch.
limitations: Only three pouches of one Nestlé product were tested. The report says tentative identification of polyethylene does not prove migration from the pouch; other contamination sources cannot be ruled out. The method detected particles above 20 μm. No clinical health outcome was measured.
